root_cause.text: The `amdxdna_get_ubuf` function in the AMD XDNA driver fails to validate that the cumulative sum of virtual address entry lengths (`va_ent[i].len`) does not overflow the `exp_info.size` variable, leading to an undersized buffer allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the unchecked addition `exp_info.size += va_ent[i].len;` with a `check_add_overflow` check in `drivers/accel/amdxdna/amdxdna_ubuf.c` to prevent integer overflow and return `-EINVAL` if an overflow is detected.

Author: Lizhi Hou <lizhi.hou@amd.com>

    accel/amdxdna: Support user space allocated buffer
    
    Enhance DRM_IOCTL_AMDXDNA_CREATE_BO to accept user space allocated
    buffer pointer. The buffer pages will be pinned in memory. Unless
    the CAP_IPC_LOCK is enabled for the application process, the total
    pinned memory can not beyond rlimit_memlock.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `amdxdna_get_ubuf` accumulates the size of virtual address entries in `exp_info.size += va_ent[i].len` (lines 173-183) without checking for integer overflow. This overflowed size is then used to calculate `ubuf->nr_pages` (line 185) and allocate the `ubuf->pages` array (line 195). During the pinning loop (lines 201-214), `pin_user_pages_fast` writes to `&ubuf->pages[start]` using the actual un-overflowed sizes, leading to an out-of-bounds write.
